business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Consignment and Secondhand Luxury Goods Retail

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Unitary national jurisdiction; no separate sub-state tax distinction for S.L. incorporation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental European codified system; Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Ley de Sociedades de Capital)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain-Mexico BIT (1996) and Spain-Mexico DTA (1994, with 2015 Protocol)
Spain-Chile DTA (2003) and EU-Chile Advanced Framework Agreement (provisionally applied 2023)
Spain-Colombia DTA (2005) and EU-Colombia/Peru/Ecuador Trade Agreement (in force 2013/2017)
EU-Mercosur Association Agreement (signed 2019, pending ratification) covering trade in goods and services
Spain-Brazil DTA (1974) and bilateral investment promotion arrangements via EU instruments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (BOE-A-2010-6738); Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 (BOE-A-2014-5040); Real Decreto-Ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, creating the Single Real Beneficiary Register (Registro de Titularidades Reales) transposing EU Directive (EU) 2018/843; Article 4.2.b RDL 7/2021 setting the 25% ownership/control disclosure threshold; relevant SEPBLAC guidelines and Spanish Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) implementing circulars.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostillized certified copy of passport of each foreign individual shareholder/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostillized certificate of good standing / certificate of legal existence (for any corporate shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry or equivalent corporate registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostillized power of attorney (Poder Especial) for incorporation and notary execution when a non-resident shareholder is not physically in Spain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Spanish translation (traducción jurada) of all non-Spanish apostilled documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator appointed by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs / accredited by an official translation institute
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification of translator signature (no Apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form (Declaración de Titularidad Real) attached to the notarial incorporation deed and filed with the Commercial Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish Notary (Notario) and Registro Mercantil Provincial
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and registry filing (no consular/Apostille path)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP identification and enhanced due diligence under Article 14 Ley 10/2010 and Article 24 RD 304/2014, covering Spanish and EU senior officials, domestic autonomous-community office holders, and international organization senior posts; mandatory screening of all shareholders/UBOs and beneficial controllers of the S.L. against the consolidated EU Financial Sanctions Database, UN Security Council consolidated lists, the SEPBLAC PEP list, and OFAC SDN/Non-SDN lists where USD-denominated payment rails (Stripe, Escrow_Pay) or US nexus transactions are processed; ongoing transaction monitoring, risk-rating refresh at minimum every 3 years, and immediate re-screening upon any ownership change; retail cash transaction limit of EUR 1,000 (EUR 10,000 where the customer is a non-resident foreigner) under Ley 7/2012.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - official name clearance via https://www.rmc.es and the Ministry of Justice online portal; notarial/electronic submission through the CIRCE or the SOIVRE-free digital channel.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name (denominación social) must be expressed in Spanish or in any official co-official language of the Kingdom (Catalan, Galician, Basque); foreign-language words are admitted only where they are techno-logical, nickname or internationally recognized terms transliterated into Latin script, and the full name must otherwise be readily pronounceable and consistent with Spanish registry transliteration rules.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España / Estado / Gobierno / Ministerio / Real / Municipal / Consejo (terms suggesting official or public status requiring prior authorization from the Council of Ministers or the corresponding public institution)
Banco / Caja / Seguros / Reaseguros / Entidad Financiera (regulated financial terms requiring express supervisory authorization)
S.A. / Sociedad Anónima / Sociedad Comanditaria / Cooperativa / Fundación / Asociación / Colegio Profesional (corporate-type tokens inconsistent with S.L. status or reserved for other legal forms)
Cruz Roja / ONU / UEFA / international organization names and protected international emblems
Names of living natural persons without documentary consent, or names of trademark right holders without proper trademark licence evidence
Denominaciones contrarias to law, morality, public order, or that mislead as to the object or nature of the company (e.g., 'investment bank' in a secondhand retail company)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The negative name certificate is valid for 3 months; if the deed is not executed within that period, a fresh certificate must be requested (no statutory automatic extension, although urgent re-issuance is available at the same fee). Upon rejection, the applicant may (i) submit an alternative denomination through the same RMC portal, or (ii) file an administrative appeal — 'recurso de alzada' — within one month before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) of the Ministry of Justice, pursuant to Articles 121-122 of Ley 39/2015; the applicant may simultaneously reserve a secondary backup name. If the alzada is denied, a further judicial appeal ('recurso contencioso-administrativo') may be lodged with the Audiencia Nacional within two months of notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not accepted as the sole registered office: the notarial deed requires a physical address (domicilio social) where the actual management or principal operations are situated (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Article 9). For an online vintage luxury resale business, a serviced office/co-working address with physical meeting space and mail acceptance is generally acceptable to the notary and registry; purely virtual mail-forwarding or P.O.-box addresses are rejected, and a residential-home registered office may be used subject to proof of legal title and municipal activity compatibility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-Low quantified risk: approximately 10-20% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Agencia Tributaria (AEAT) or SEPBLAC within the first 24 months of operation, driven primarily by VAT registration thresholds, cross-border payment volume, and any flags on the commercial substance profile; a genuine serviced-office address, bookkeeping records, and active logistics contracts reduce this risk to the lower end of the range.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social) from Registro Mercantil Central
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central — Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fee schedule published in BOE; approx. EUR 41 for standard processing, with optional 24-hour expedite fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución) including UBO declaration annex
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee scale per Orden JUS/329/2016; prevailing benchmark for a standard S.L. with EUR 3,000 capital and one corporate object, range EUR 550-750

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank certificate of capital contribution deposit (Certificado de Desembolso Bancario) in a blocked S.L. pre-incorporation account
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank administrative fee; prevailing market benchmark EUR 35-60 depending on bank

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial Registry inscription (Inscripción de la Sociedad en el Registro Mercantil Provincial)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official BOE-tariff calculated on share capital and number of registry entries; approx. EUR 110 for a EUR 3,000 capital S.L.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) processing for non-resident shareholders via consular authority or authorized representative
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Consulate / Dirección General de Policía (via representative)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee (modelo 790-012, approx. EUR 10) plus representative and courier benchmark of EUR 70-90

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille / consular legalization bundle for foreign shareholder passports, corporate certificates, and powers of attorney (estimated 4-6 documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Delegación del Gobierno / competent Apostille authority in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of EUR 25-45 per apostilled document, inclusive of courier and administrative handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation (traducción jurada) of apostilled non-Spanish documents into Spanish
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official translator tariff of EUR 30-45 per page; estimated 3-4 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT onboarding package — PEP and sanctions screening (World-Check / Dow Jones or equivalent) plus S.L. AML policy manual and UBO piercing report
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial compliance data provider / legal AML consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual screening subscription (EUR 200-300) plus fixed compliance drafting fee (approx. EUR 50-100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-month registered office service (serviced office / domiciliación postal with physical acceptance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 100-250 per month in Madrid or Barcelona for a physical co-working registered address

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Electronic incorporation filing and procedural fee (CIRCE/TAE or notarial online processing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Minimal statutory telematics charge; benchmark EUR 20-30 per submission

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act, including Articles 4, 19-22, 23-30, 32-35, 58-62, 159-160, 210-212, 214-217, 225-232 and 246-251; Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Commercial Registry Regulations; Law 14/2013 on support for entrepreneurs and internationalization for CIRCE and electronic incorporation procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated where applicable through the Central Mercantile Registry and the CIRCE/PAE electronic system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), together with the approved articles of association, filed for registration with the competent Provincial Commercial Registry. The registered company is issued a permanent tax identification number by the Spanish Tax Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The statutory minimum share capital of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and fully paid at incorporation. Until share capital reaches EUR 3,000, at least 20% of annual profits must be allocated to a legal reserve until the reserve plus capital reaches EUR 3,000, and shareholders have subsidiary liability for the difference between EUR 3,000 and the subscribed capital in specified liquidation circumstances. There is no general statutory escrow requirement; funds may be paid into a company account or otherwise evidenced before execution of the deed, subject to notarial requirements.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board resolves that: (1) the shares subscribed by the founder or founders are confirmed as fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted; (3) [name] is appointed sole director, or [names] are appointed as joint or several directors, as applicable, each accepting office and declaring no statutory disqualification; (4) [name] is appointed attorney-in-fact for tax, registry, banking and licensing filings; and (5) the officers are authorized to obtain the NIF, open bank accounts, execute commercial contracts and complete all post-incorporation registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its online name-certification service or an authorized filing channel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, preferably including the legal suffix Sociedad Limitada or S.L. Obtain the negative name certificate and ensure that the certificate remains valid for execution of the incorporation deed. Preserve the original electronic certificate for the notary and registry filing.
required_dossiers: Up to five proposed company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or request a corrected certificate. If the certificate expires, obtain a new certificate before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Identification and Tax Credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Administration (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), through Form 036, and the competent police or consular channel for foreigner identification numbers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain an NIE for each non-resident individual director, shareholder or authorized representative requiring Spanish tax identification. Obtain an NIF for each non-resident corporate shareholder and evidence of its existence, ownership and authority. Apostille or legalize foreign public documents and provide sworn Spanish translations where required.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate certificates of incorporation and good standing
Corporate resolutions approving the investment and representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure missing legalization, translation, identity or beneficial-owner information and resubmit to the Tax Administration or police/consular authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary selected by the incorporator, with tax and registry forms prepared through the notary, CIRCE/PAE system or professional representative.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association, ownership percentages, share capital, management structure, registered office, corporate purpose and beneficial-owner statement. For an online resale business, define the corporate purpose to cover ecommerce, retail, consignment, acquisition and resale of secondhand goods, logistics and related services, subject to any regulated activity exclusions. Obtain a bank certificate of capital deposit if requested by the notary; the certificate may be omitted where legally permitted if founders assume the statutory contribution liability.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent corporate purpose, ownership, capital, address or authority information before the notarial appointment. Replace defective powers or obtain supplemental shareholder resolutions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (Notario) within the relevant notarial district.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear personally or through a properly legalized power of attorney. Execute the public incorporation deed, articles and beneficial-owner declarations. Confirm the management model and appointment of directors. The notary verifies identity, capacity, authority, legality and capital contribution evidence, and may submit the deed electronically to the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Original or certified negative name certificate
Capital payment certificate or permitted alternative declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address notarial observations immediately, provide missing originals or translations, and execute a corrective deed where an error has already been signed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional NIF and Register the Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Administration for the provisional NIF and the Provincial Commercial Registry for incorporation registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 036 and the notarial deed to obtain the provisional NIF. Submit the authorized electronic copy or certified deed to the Provincial Commercial Registry with the required registry forms and fees. Monitor the registry entry and obtain the registered deed and registry information. Registration creates the company's full commercial publicity and confirms its corporate standing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification note, cure each defect within the applicable period, submit a corrected document or appeal the qualification to the Directorate-General for Legal Certainty and Public Faith where appropriate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Beneficial-Owner and Social Security Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Administration, Commercial Registry and Spanish Social Security Administration (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convert the provisional NIF into the definitive NIF after registration. Register the applicable economic activities and tax obligations, including VAT and corporate tax. Maintain beneficial-owner information and obtain the ultimate beneficial-owner certification required by banks, notaries and regulated counterparties. Register the company as an employer before hiring personnel and affiliate directors or employees where legally required.
required_dossiers: Definitive registry certificate or registry data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend Form 036 or registry data, provide missing beneficial-owner evidence and correct Social Security classification before commencing employment or payroll activity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Corporate Books and Governance Controls
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Commercial Registry for legalization of corporate books; company board and shareholders for internal approvals.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Acquire and electronically legalize the shareholders' register, minutes book, contracts with the sole shareholder where applicable, and other mandatory books. Approve the first board resolution, director remuneration policy where relevant, signing authorities, related-party procedures and accounting controls. File annual accounts and the annual corporate documents within statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective minutes or book entries through a subsequent properly approved resolution and submit corrected electronic books or annual filings within the applicable cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Municipal Activity and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ayuntamiento of the municipality where the registered operating premises, warehouse or retail location is situated, together with the applicable autonomous-community authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the premises require a responsible declaration, prior communication, opening license, activity license or works permit. File the applicable municipal application before commencing operations at the premises. For an online resale model using third-party logistics without owned premises, document the exemption or allocation of responsibility and verify the provider's permits.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal technical observations, amend the technical report or works documentation, and do not open the premises until the required declaration, communication or license is effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No general national industrial manufacturing license applies to online consignment and secondhand luxury-goods resale. Premises-related competence rests principally with the relevant Ayuntamiento and, where applicable, the industrial, environmental and consumer authority of the autonomous community.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal responsible declaration or prior communication for activity and opening (declaración responsable or comunicación previa de actividad y apertura), or municipal activity and opening license where required by the applicable autonomous-community and local rules.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental body of the relevant autonomous community, applying Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a project-level EIA for ordinary ecommerce, consignment and resale operations without industrial processing, significant emissions or listed infrastructure. A screening or full assessment may apply if the premises or project falls within a statutory Annex I or Annex II category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with municipal and autonomous-community wastewater discharge rules; obtain authorization for any non-domestic discharge where required. Avoid unpermitted VOC or combustion emissions. Store, classify and transfer packaging, electronic, textile, hazardous or other regulated waste through authorized waste managers. Fulfil applicable extended producer responsibility and packaging obligations, including Royal Decree 1055/2022 where the company places packaged products on the Spanish market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before operating a warehouse, showroom or office, verify municipal fire-safety compliance under the Spanish Building Code and applicable fire protection regulations, maintain extinguishers, emergency routes, signage and evacuation procedures, and obtain any required technical certificate or opening clearance. Confirm structural load, electrical and installation compliance where applicable. Complete occupational risk assessment and prevention arrangements under Law 31/1995, including employee training, emergency planning, workplace health and safety controls, and contractor coordination.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Tax Agency of Spain; online portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Before formal incorporation of a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL), the foreign investor or legal representative obtains a provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT using form 036. Following incorporation and notarial registration, the provisional NIF is converted to a definitive NIF assigned to the SL. The company must be registered in the Spanish Central Register of Companies (Registro Mercantil Central) and, for VAT purposes, complete form 036 to declare commencement of activity and obtain a Spanish VAT identification number. Where services or goods are received from abroad, an indirect representation regime may apply until the definitive NIF is granted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for a domestic SL; the SL is invariably treated as a resident corporation liable to Spanish Corporate Income Tax at 25% (reduced rates for newly created SMEs and certain activities). Hybrid mismatch rules apply under Spanish law (Law 27/2014, as amended) to neutralize mismatches in line with ATAD, including election-like adjustments for hybrid instruments and reverse hybrid entities, but no check-the-box regime comparable to the US exists for domestic Spanish entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration exemption threshold for corporations; any person or entity carrying out taxable economic activities in Spain must register for VAT regardless of turnover. Small Business exemptions are limited to the Simplified Regime (Régimen Simplificado) and the Rebate Regime (Régimen de Recargo de Equivalencia) for specified retailers, subject to an annual turnover limit of €250,000 for the Simplified Regime, but such regimes do not waive registration; they are optional simplified calculation methods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing is mandatory in the B2B sector under the 'Crea y Crece' Law (Law 18/2022), with acceptance by the recipient and interoperability obligations phased in for large enterprises (starting 2024) and all businesses by 2025; invoices must be issued in a structured electronic format. For VAT information reporting, large companies, Group VAT registrations, and certain other taxpayers must submit sales and purchase records electronically in near real-time through the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system to AEAT within four business days of invoicing. The future Verifactu system (RD 1007/2023) will require compliant billing software to produce integrity-protected, unalterable invoice records and transmit them to AEAT where required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Spanish territory to destinations outside the EU and to the Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla qualify for VAT zero-rating under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law (Law 37/1992). Supply of services linked to exported goods and certain services rendered to non-EU businesses or non-resident entrepreneurs may also be zero-rated or subject to the reverse charge where the recipient is taxable abroad; the supplier must possess substantial documentary evidence establishing the physical dispatch or transport out of the EU and the objective nature of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA/SAD) with validation by Spanish Customs (AEAT EX) showing dispatch outside the EU
Commercial Invoice in original and copies
Bill of Lading (B/L), Air Waybill (AWB), or CMR transport document evidencing export movement
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/FX settlement proof for the export consideration
Intrastat/Extrastat declaration where applicable, and the documentary support required under Article 66 of the Spanish VAT Regulation
Agent/authorized representative authorization form if customs clearance was performed through a proxy
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims for VAT zero-rating on exports are subject to intensive AEAT audit review, including verification of the physical exit of goods through customs records and the authenticity of transport documents. Where documentation is incomplete or false, the AEAT will retroactively require VAT at the applicable Spanish rate (21%) for the supply, plus late-payment interest from the date of invoicing. Under the Spanish General Tax Law (Ley 58/2003, Art. 184 and 191), penalty assessments range from 50% to 150% of the undeclared VAT amount depending on fraudulent intent; willful omission or use of forged export documents may constitute an infraction of Article 191 or tax offence (Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code) with imprisonment from one to five years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount. Repatriation of export proceeds beyond a reasonable period (in practice scrutinized after 180 days) without satisfactory justification is treated as strong evidence of domestic final disposal, triggering clawback of zero-rating and associated penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is the prudential regulator, statistical hub and supervisory authority for credit institutions and e-money institutions; the Foreign Exchange Administration for capital-movement compliance is the Secretariat of State for Commerce (Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones) under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism, applying Law 19/2003 (movements of capital and economic transactions with foreign countries), Law 18/1992 (foreign investment) and Royal Decree 664/1999. The Council of Ministers retains protective suspension powers under Law 19/2003 Art. 7 bis for sectors of critical security, public order or health — not applicable to ISIC 4791 online luxury resale.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is the domestic currency and is fully convertible; Spain applies the TFEU Art. 63 free-movement-of-capital regime for both EU and non-EU capital flows with no general approval, no exchange-control quotas and no restrictions on current-account or capital-account transactions. Non-residents may own 100% of an ES_SL without exchange-control permission. Practical hurdles: (1) post-event statistical declarations to Banco de España for inward/outward settlements ≥ EUR 50,000; (2) filing the foreign-investment declaration with the Registry of Foreign Investments within 30 days; (3) a 19% non-resident dividend withholding tax on profit remittance (treaty relief possible) applied and declared via Modelo 216; and (4) the need to identify the account holder and UBO under AML Law 10/2010. There is neither a 'dilution' nor a 'prior import licence' concern for e-commerce receivables.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender rule and no mandatory conversion ratio applies to Spanish exporters; export proceeds in any currency may be retained in foreign-currency accounts, reinvested abroad or remitted in EUR at the exporter's discretion within EU BOP liberalisation. Administrative obligations: (i) the receiving bank aggregates the entity's cross-border settlements (SEPA/SWIFT) and furnishes the monthly balance-of-payments declaration to Banco de España under Circular 4/2004; (ii) each shipment of vintage luxury goods must be supported by a compliant commercial invoice, packing list and, for exports outside the EU, Intrastat/Extrastat data or customs EX-A registry — but no FX conversion document is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability: MEDIUM for day-to-day receivables and operational expenses in EUR, LOW-MEDIUM for capital escrow, inventory settlements and high-value consignor payouts. Legal constraints: a viable FinTech must be a licensed e-money institution (EMI) or payment institution (PI) in an EEA state and passport under PSD2/EMD2 to Spain through the Banco de España register; its safeguarding obligations under Art. 7 of EMD2 and collection of customer funds must be fully segregated. However, under Spanish AML Law 10/2010, high-value luxury resale is designated as an increased-risk activity; several EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Qonto, Monese) restrict the onboarding of luxury resale merchants, apply operation limits (EUR 5,000–25,000 monthly), or request supplier and authentication documentation. They may also decline any escrow structure of third-party funds because the SL has no payment-institution licence. Therefore, use a Tier-1 bank as the primary clearing and custody bank, with EMI services limited to card acquiring payouts (Stripe) and marginal FX.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate opening is exceptional; the administrator (administrador único) or a jointly authorised director must normally physically attend a branch in Spain to sign the account-opening mandate and be identified personally. Alternative: grant a notarised power of attorney (poder notarial) before a Spanish notary or a Spanish consulate abroad in favour of an accredited Spanish legal representative, followed by a compliance interview — many Tier-1 banks accept this without the attorney being physically present if the power is apostilled and translated. Non-EEA directors must obtain a NIE and, in most banks, the signature of the legal representative is taken at the first face-to-face visit. The onboarding dossier must include: notarised and apostilled certificate shares of the SL (escritura de constitución), tax identification (NIF/CIF provisional), company address proof, UBO declarations, business plan with expected turnover, and proof of settlement rails (Stripe/Escrow_Pay contracts); a video-identification tool is allowed only for the individual board member as part of the bank's online onboarding for SLs with purely EU/EEA ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA shareholders and beneficial owners domiciled in Latin America (especially high-risk jurisdictions) without a visible economic nexus.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) certified apostilled constitutional documents, statutory registers and full UBO organigram (25%+ owners); (2) NIE/tax ID of the SL and of each director; (3) source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statement executed before a notary, with bank reference letters from the UBO's local bank; (4) official extract of criminal records (antecedentes penales) from the UBO's country of origin or embassy certificate; (5) PEP self-declaration with an explanation of any political exposure; (6) a Spanish legal opinion confirming the foreign investments comply with Law 19/2003 and RD 664/1999.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume online resale of luxury vintage goods creating heterogeneous invoice values, chargeback risk and typical money-laundering typology (over/under-invoicing).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) independent authentication certificates for each high-ticket item (Entrupy, Authenticate First, Vestiaire Collective or auction-house dossier); (2) acquisition/final-sale invoices from consignors, estates and auctions; (3) valuation or expert appraisal (tasación) by a registered valuator; (4) marketplace merchant agreements (Stripe, Escrow_Pay) describing settlement, refund, chargeback and fee flows; (5) a signed 'Know Your Consignor' SOP and AML risk assessment under Law 10/2010; (6) a transaction-level data room (buyer/seller/ITS) accessible to the bank's compliance analyst for the first 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Indication that the SL acts as an unlicensed payment intermediary or money-service business because consignment sales produce third-party payouts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) the principal-based resale contract model (the SL acquires legal title and settles its suppliers after margin), supported by general terms of sale; (2) legal opinion confirming the business is trade in goods under ISIC 4791 and not an 'acceptance of funds to execute payment transactions' under PSD2; (3) settlement schedules proving each disbursement is connected to an underlying purchase invoice and inventory movement; (4) the commerce register statement; (5) initial capital and escrow account details evidencing equity as the sole funding source for operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border movements Spain–US–Latin America with SEPA/SWIFT transfers in multiple currencies and no prior banking relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bundle: (1) three-year audited cash-flow forecast and business plan linking target rails (Stripe to the operational account, Escrow_Pay as service); (2) first-year transaction forecasting (number of items, average ticket, expected FX); (3) executed CAP/OPEX budget; (4) certificate of initial equity deposit; (5) evidence of compliance with the balance-of-payments declaration (Circular 4/2004) and, if applicable, tax residency of the shareholders; (6) the legal entity's IBAN only for the beneficial owner and no third-party collection accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execution protocol: the non-resident shareholder wire-transfers the equity subscription exclusively to the segregated 'cuenta de capital' (capital account) of the ES_SL via SWIFT MT103 with UETR; the bank is instructed to apply the payment to capital formation, and the funds may not be released until the constitution deed is registered in the Registro Mercantil and a certificate of deposit is issued. Use the ISO 20022 SEPA/SWIFT purpose code 'CCAP' (contribution to capital) or 'ENTR' (equity injection) and insert in field 72 the legal reference: '/DEA/Aportación de capital social a ES_SL conforme RD 664/1999 y Ley 19/2003'. Within 30 days of the transfer, the non-resident shareholder must file the foreign-investment declaration in the Registro de Inversiones Exteriores using the Ministry's electronic portal and identify the Spanish company and the amount; the bank will issue a certificate of inward capital for that statement. If the wire is made in USD, the FX desk converts via the agreed spot and the converted EUR is credited — the conversion provisions and FX rate will be documented. The bank may request the company's purpose, the shareholder resolution, UBO details and beneficiary ownership before activation; the capital account cannot be used for trade disbursements until the SL is registered and the bank executes the operational account resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail for payments is SWIFT MT103 (EUR/USD) for non-EEA suppliers, with UETR tracker and explicit 'Beneficiary' identity matching the purchase invoice. For EUR settlements inside the SEPA zone, use SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst / pain.001.001.09) with ISO purpose code 'GOOD' or 'GDDS'; the due-diligence file retains the acquisition invoice and authentication certificate. For high-value acquisition of entire collections (≥ EUR 50,000), a commercial letter of credit under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700/MT710) is permissible if the beneficiary presents the bill of lading/warehouse certificate, signed commercial invoices and authentication report, with a correspondent/collecting-bank confirmation for LatAm sellers. Consignor (seller) payouts are made from the operational account after the sale, with each transfer linked to a unique trade ID and effective on delivery/acceptance and returns processing. Escrow/Pay (third-party) rails are legally viable only if the provider holds client funds in segregated accounts under EMD2/PSD2; for large seller balances, use a nested escrow account in the Tier-1 bank. Timelines: SCT Inst clears <10 sec; SEPA CT T+1; SWIFT (US) T+1/T+2; FX settlement T+2; all transactions are aggregated in the monthly BOP report of the bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL, EUR/CLP, EUR/COP) executed on ISDA/CSA documentation with MiFID II-licensed Spanish banks or EU broker-dealers; hedging of underlying commercial exposure only.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) referencing restricted LatAm currencies (EUR/ARS, EUR/VES, EUR/CUP) settled in EUR or USD cash on reference (e.g., WM/Refinitiv) rate, available with credit lines from Tier-1 domestic banks.

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) EUR/USD for long-term procurement flows from the US marketplace (Stripe/USD accounts), with mandatory EMIR reporting via ESMA-approved trade repository and, if above clearing threshold, central clearing.

Vanilla FX options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) and EUR/MXN option structures covering seasonal inventory purchases; premiums booked as treasury expense; all operations under EMIR and MiFID II conduct rules; Modelo 720 reporting required if any foreign-currency account or instrument held abroad exceeds EUR 50,000 year-end.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT summary return (Declaración-Resumen Anual del IVA, Form 390)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January after the close of the calendar tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing accrues late-payment surcharges of 5% to 20% depending on delay, plus late-payment interest; inaccurate or incomplete data triggers penalties of 50% of the understated tax with a minimum of EUR 150.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third‑party transactions return (Declaración de operaciones con terceras personas, Form 347)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 20 March following the calendar year; mandatory when aggregate transactions with any single counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06 in the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing carries fines of EUR 150 to EUR 750 per data item; omission of transactions may be penalised with 50% of the aggregate undeclared amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of statutory accounting books (Legalización de los libros obligatorios: Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) matching the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the four months following the annual balance-sheet date; by 30 April for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unlegalized books carry no evidentiary value before commercial judges; continued omission may give rise to ICAC inspection warnings and may block the deposit of the annual accounts until regularised.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Form 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days after the seven months following the tax-period start; for a calendar-year company from 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs surcharge of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% depending on the delay, plus interest for late payment; false or misleading data can produce penalties up to 150% of the resulting tax deficiency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (Depósito de cuentas anuales) comprising the balance sheet, profit-and-loss account, statement of changes in equity, notes, and auditor's report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the shareholders' meeting approving the accounts; approval must occur within six months from the year-end, giving an outer deadline of 30 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) preventing registration of any later corporate act until deposit is made; administrative penalties of EUR 1,200 to EUR 10,000; repeated non-deposit for three consecutive years exposes the company to a commercial-dissolution procedure before the Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual update of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner registry declaration (Actualización anual de titulares reales / beneficiarios finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Titularidades Reales operated through the Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the annual accounts deposit; same outer limit of 30 July for a 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete or update the UBO declaration is a breach of Law 10/2010 on money laundering; serious infringements carry fines ranging from EUR 60,000 to EUR 300,000, and the annual accounts deposit may be rejected until regularised.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies when the company exceeds at least two of the following for two consecutive years on the balance-sheet date: (a) total assets over EUR 2,850,000; (b) net annual turnover over EUR 5,700,000; (c) average workforce above 50 employees. Audit may also be requested by shareholders holding at least 5% of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (Plan General de Contabilidad, RD 1514/2007), interpreted by the Instituto de Contabilidad y Auditoría de Cuentas (ICAC); individual accounts use local GAAP, whereas consolidated groups apply IFRS as endorsed by the EU.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The directors must keep an internal register of ultimate beneficial owners and submit an updated annual declaration together with the deposit of annual accounts. Any share transfer identifying a new UBO with a direct or indirect shareholding or control of 25% or more must be reflected in that annual confirmation; changes in between annual filings are confirmed at the next annual submission.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and board appointments (Registro de consejeros / acuerdos de nombramiento)
Accounting ledgers (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales) kept at the registered office with legalized covers

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,800 (typical annual registered-office and corporate-compliance agent market rate in Spain)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,600 - 4,000 (typical certified audit fee for a small-to-medium SL; audit may be waived below the legal thresholds)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% for newly created entities during the first two years of taxable income (subject to conditions). Tax credits for R&D, export activities, and reinvestment of profits. No specific sectoral holiday for luxury resale.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) online portal (www.agenciatributaria.es)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year entities, deadline is 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income unless PE exemption applies; for non-resident entities with PE, allocate income to PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate (25% or reduced 15% for new entities)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply standard rate unless treaty or special regime applies.
Calculate based on taxable income and rate.
Claim only those available under domestic law or treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of tax due if filed within 30 days of deadline; 10% within 6 months; 15% within 12 months; 20% after 12 months. Fixed penalty of €200 for late filing without tax due. Surcharge for late payment: 5% to 20% depending on delay.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding under a Double Tax Agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficiary must submit a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, and file Form 210 (Non-Resident Income Tax) or use the streamlined procedure via the AEAT. The payer must retain the TRC and apply the treaty rate at source. For EU/EEA entities, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive may allow 0% withholding if conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory rate 24%; treaty rates typically 5-10%. Interest: statutory rate 19%; treaty rates often 0-10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 10,000,000 net turnover triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation. Transactions with related parties exceeding EUR 250,000 per category also require documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain applies substance-over-form principles and has Controlled Foreign Corporation (CFC) rules. Entities must demonstrate real economic activity (personnel, assets, risks) to avoid recharacterization or anti-abuse measures. No specific ESR regime, but general anti-abuse rules and the 'business purpose' doctrine apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false invoicing, or concealment of assets to reduce tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 50% to 150% of the evaded tax, plus interest. Criminal prosecution for amounts exceeding EUR 120,000 per year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for unpaid corporate taxes if they knowingly participated in evasion. Civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without real business activity, employees, or physical presence, solely to obtain tax benefits or avoid reporting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of tax benefits, recharacterization of transactions, and potential application of anti-abuse rules. Fines up to EUR 150,000 for non-compliance with substance requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for taxes and penalties if they knowingly used a shell structure. Travel bans and disqualification from holding directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement AML controls, accepting cash payments above EUR 10,000, or failing to report suspicious transactions in the luxury resale sector.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 5 million or 10% of turnover for serious breaches. Criminal liability for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can face imprisonment (up to 6 years) and personal fines. Travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation, or applying non-arm's length prices in cross-border transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 15% on the adjusted amount, and interest. For documentation failure, penalty of EUR 1,000 per data item, up to EUR 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held liable for penalties if they approved or ignored TP violations. Civil liability for damages to the tax authority.
